transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because things I usually enjoy have started feeling flat and heavy. I used to take photography walks, mentor the kids, keep my calendar organized—now I just don’t initiate any of it. It doesn’t feel like me.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, or has it been going on more continuously for a year or more?
It’s been more continuous—about a year and three months now. It started after a family member’s health and behavior changed, and I ended up taking on a lot more of the coordination.
Since this began, have you had any distinct periods—lasting several days—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, I do have stretches where I feel unusually upbeat, like everything is clicking and I’m really sure of myself. But then something small—like someone moving a meeting—can set me off, and I get sharp with people in a way that surprises me.
When you have those upbeat, energized stretches, how many days in a row do they typically last?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t kept track of the number of days—I just notice I’m more up and reactive for a while, then it fades.
Have you noticed any physical changes recently, like unexplained weight gain, feeling unusually cold, dry skin, or constipation?
I haven’t really noticed any physical changes like that. Nothing stands out to me recently.
Besides the low mood and loss of interest, have you noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, concentration, or energy that occur nearly every day during this time?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether those things are changing every day.
Has there been a period of at least two straight weeks where this low, flat mood was so intense that it seriously interfered with your ability to work or manage daily responsibilities?

I don’t know if I could say it was two straight weeks exactly, but it got to where I stopped initiating things I normally care about—my photography walks, mentoring the kids, even keeping my calendar organized. Everything just felt flat and heavy.

Since this began about 15 months ago, has your low, flat mood been present more days than not, without any stretches of feeling essentially back to your normal self, or have there been clear breaks where the low mood lifted completely for weeks at a time?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t tracked it closely enough to know whether there were weeks where I felt fully back to normal.
During those upbeat, energized stretches, have people around you noticed a clear change in your behavior or mood compared to your usual self?

Yeah, I think so. I can get unusually upbeat, like everything is really clicking, and then something small—someone moving a meeting, for example—can make me snap or get sharp with people. It surprises me afterward.
When you notice these upbeat, energized periods, do they typically last at least four days in a row, or are they usually shorter—just a day or two?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t paid enough attention to how many days they last to say whether it’s four days or just a day or two.
During those upbeat, energized stretches, do you find you need noticeably less sleep than usual but still feel rested and full of energy?
Yes. There have been nights when I only sleep two or three hours, wake up before dawn, and feel ready to start answering emails or updating appointment lists instead of feeling tired.

Thinking about the last time you had one of these upbeat, high-energy stretches with little need for sleep, can you recall whether it lasted through most of a week, or did it fade after just a day or two?
It hasn’t just been a day or two. These stretches have been coming back on and off for about eleven months now—the high energy, barely sleeping, feeling overly confident.

Focusing on your lowest periods, can you tell me if there was ever a stretch of at least two full weeks in a row where you felt this flat, heavy mood nearly every single day, without any days of feeling essentially normal?
I’m not really sure. I know I’ve had low periods, but I haven’t tracked whether they went on for two full weeks straight without any better days.

Since these mood changes began about 15 months ago, has there ever been a stretch of two months or longer where you felt essentially like your normal self, without the low, flat periods or the upbeat, energized periods?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really kept track well enough to know whether there was a full two-month stretch where I felt completely back to normal.

During your lowest periods, was there ever a stretch of at least two consecutive weeks where the flat, heavy mood caused you to actually miss work, skip important commitments, or fail to keep up with basic responsibilities every single day?

Not every day, no. I’ve kept working overall, though I’ve missed some calendar details and had to double-check things that used to be automatic. I’ve pulled back from photography outings and mentoring because I don’t feel as present or reliable.

During those upbeat, high-energy stretches, has anyone—coworkers, family, or friends—ever told you that your behavior was so different that it caused real problems, like conflicts at work or noticeable disruption to your relationships?

Yeah, I think people have noticed I can be pretty different. I’ll feel unusually upbeat, like everything is clicking, but then something small—like somebody moving a meeting—can set me off, and I get sharp with people. It surprises me afterward.
Think about the most recent time you had one of these energized, barely-sleeping stretches—can you tell me, day by day, how many days in a row it lasted before you went back to your usual self?
I can’t really count it day by day. Those stretches have been coming and going for about eleven months now—feeling more driven, sleeping less, and having more confidence than usual.

Looking back over the past 15 months, can you identify any single two-month stretch—say a specific two-month period you can pinpoint—where you felt fully like your normal, stable self, with neither the low, flat mood nor the upbeat, energized episodes at all?

No, I don’t think I can point to a full two months like that. Even when there are quieter weeks, I seem to cycle back into feeling driven and overconfident, sleeping less, and taking on more than I should.
